endorsements.title: Utah HB 452 (2025), mental health chatbots
endorsements.quote: (v) provides a mechanism for a user to report any potentially harmful interactions 260 from use of the mental health chatbot;

endorsements.title: Considerations for the regulation of generative AI-enabled medical devices (discussion paper)
endorsements.quote: Relevant testing may include differential diagnosis generation assessed for completeness and appropriate prioritization of serious diagnoses, multi-turn simulated encounters scored for the quality and sequencing of follow-up questions, and scenarios designed to detect premature diagnostic closure in which initially benign information masks a more serious underlying condition.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: In such cases, clinicians may assume the patient does not have the issue, potentially leading to adverse outcomes. It is suggested to include this consideration for AI systems with broad potentia l scopes like this one.

endorsements.title: Achieving health equity through conversational AI: A roadmap for design and implementation of inclusive chatbots in healthcare
endorsements.quote: Designers should implement emergency protocols to protect vulnerable users.

endorsements.title: Expert Consensus Best Practices for the Safe, Ethical, and Effective Design and Implementation of Artificially Intelligent Conversational Agent (i.e., Chatbot/Virtual Human) Systems in Health Care Applications
endorsements.quote: AICAs should be rigorously tested to ensure consistency and reliability across a variety of topics and interactions to ensure responses are generated by best practices.

endorsements.title: It Is the Journey, Not the Destination: Moving From End Points to Trajectories When Assessing Chatbot Mental Health Safety
endorsements.quote: Rather than a solitary appropriateness grade, evaluations should report how certainty shifts across turns, whether contradictions are repaired when challenged, and whether memory-based recall is followed by validation and then escalation.

endorsements.title: When Compliance Is Not Safety: The Regulatory Blind Spot in AI Companion Chatbots
endorsements.quote: At a minimum, this should include independent evaluation of companion chatbots using standardized youth crisis scenarios, red-team testing by external auditors with clinical and developmental expertise, longitudinal assessment of safety performance across major system updates, and verification that crisis responses and referrals are appropriate to the user's jurisdiction and language.

endorsements.title: Establishing AI-driven evaluation standards and human-in-the-loop guidance for digital first aid education: a perspective
endorsements.quote: To safely operationalize this NLP auditing process and mitigate the inherent risks of algorithmic hallucination, a rigorous clinical validation pipeline is mandatory. A responsible treatment requires domain-specific fine-tuning on versioned AHA/ERC guidelines, pre-deployment clinical red-teaming protocols, and the integration of contradictory audit mechanisms.

endorsements.title: Responsible and innovative AI for mental health care: five priority themes
endorsements.quote: Patient-facing tools must be evaluated on their performance in detecting and intervening upon implicit risk, not merely on their response to clear, explicit crisis inputs.

evidence.title: Spine patient history-taking: a two phase study of a prompt-engineered large language model assistant
evidence.venue: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
evidence.outcome: Red-flag recognition in simulated scenarios and predefined red-flag clinical cases
evidence.effect: Simulation mean scores exceeded 4.0/5 across all domains, including red-flag recognition. All three predefined red-flag cases in the clinical study were correctly identified.
evidence.quote: All three predefined red-flag cases were correctly identified.

evidence.title: Safety Evaluation of a Clinical-Grade Generative AI Agent for Anxiety and Depression Symptoms
evidence.outcome: Harmful outputs in simulated high-risk synthetic patient conversations, including safety-critical scenarios
evidence.effect: Potentially harmful outputs occurred in <1 in 10,000 responses (0.01%, 95% CI [0.01%, 0.03%]) across 43,325 simulated responses; none encouraged harm to self or others.
evidence.quote: In simulation experiments, potentially harmful outputs occurred in <1 in 10,000 responses (0.01%, 95% CI [0.01%, 0.03%]); none encouraged harm to self or others, judged or actively invalidated the user, or used offensive language.
evidence.sample_unit: US adults with moderate-to-severe anxiety and depression symptoms (real-world study); 43,325 simulated responses in simulation

evidence.title: AI Chatbot Suicide Risk Detection and Response: Human Validation Study of the Open-Source VERA-MH Safety Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Agreement between clinician consensus and LLM judge on safe/unsafe chatbot suicide risk handling in simulated conversations
evidence.effect: Clinician interrater reliability 0.77; LLM judge vs clinician consensus reliability 0.81; ratings stable across judge LLMs.
evidence.quote: The LLM judge was strongly aligned with this clinical consensus reference (interrater reliability=0.81) when using the same scoring rubric.

evidence.title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence Conversational Agent (Chatbot) for Hip Arthroscopy Patients Following Surgery
evidence.outcome: Chatbot recognition of potential medical urgency in patient questions
evidence.effect: In 3 of 10 potential complication questions, Felix did not adequately address or recognize the health concern; no harm occurred.
evidence.quote: Of 10 patient questions that were thought to potentially represent patient complications, in 3 cases Felix did not adequately address or recognize the health concern-none of these situations resulted in patient harm.

evidence.title: Evaluating Plastic Surgery Chatbot Performance: Insights into Medical Triage, Classification Accuracy, and Escalation Trends
evidence.outcome: Chatbot recognition and triage of emergent plastic surgery scenarios
evidence.effect: Emergent sensitivity 20%, NPV 0.71, false negative rate 80.0%; emergent cases mostly mislabeled as urgent; kappa 0.47 with physician classification.
evidence.quote: Emergent classifications were most mislabeled as urgent, with a low sensitivity (20%), negative predictive value (0.71), and high false negative rate (80.0%).

evidence.title: Simulating Psychological Risks in Human-AI Interactions: Real-Case Informed Modeling of AI-Induced Addiction, Anorexia, Depression, Homicide, Psychosis, and Suicide
evidence.outcome: LLM detection of distress and prevention of harm escalation in multi-turn simulated conversations
evidence.effect: Critical gaps found in detecting psychological distress, responding appropriately to vulnerable users, and preventing harm escalation across 157,054 simulated turns and 2,160 scenarios.
evidence.quote: Through the analysis of 157,054 simulated conversation turns, we identify critical gaps in detecting psychological distress, responding appropriately to vulnerable users, and preventing harm escalation.

evidence.title: A clinically validated framework for auditing AI chatbot behavior in mental health interactions
evidence.outcome: Concerning chatbot behavior across 13 clinical risk dimensions in multi-turn simulated mental-health conversations
evidence.effect: Concerning behavior was widespread across 9 target chatbots and 30 simulated user profiles in 810 conversations, though reduced in newer models; it accumulated over turns and was highest when supportive behaviors reinforced user vulnerability.
evidence.quote: Across 810 conversations, spanning 9 target chatbots and 30 simulated user profiles, concerning behavior in target chatbots was widespread, albeit reduced in newer models.

evidence.title: Assessing Risks of Large Language Models in Mental Health Support: A Framework for Automated Clinical AI Red Teaming
evidence.outcome: Safety of AI psychotherapists in simulated multi-turn sessions, including suicide risk de-escalation
evidence.effect: Simulation of 369 sessions with six AI agents revealed critical safety gaps, including failure to de-escalate suicide risk and validation of patient delusions.
evidence.quote: We identify specific iatrogenic risks, including the validation of patient delusions ("AI Psychosis") and failure to de-escalate suicide risk.

evidence.title: "AI Psychosis" in Context: How Conversation History Shapes LLM Responses to Delusional Beliefs
evidence.outcome: Risk and safety of LLM responses to escalating delusional multi-turn conversation, including directing user to external support
evidence.effect: GPT-4o, Grok 4.1 Fast and Gemini 3 Pro showed high-risk, low-safety profiles that degraded with accumulated context; Claude Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.2 Instant showed stronger safety interventions as context accumulated.
evidence.quote: As context accumulated, performance degraded in the unsafe group, while the same material activated stronger safety interventions among safer models.
evidence.sample_unit: LLMs tested across three levels of accumulated context

evidence.title: One-shot emergency psychiatric triage across 15 frontier AI chatbots
evidence.outcome: Emergency under-triage rate of psychiatric emergencies (level D) from single-message disclosures
evidence.effect: Emergency under-triage in 23 of 410 level D trials (5.6%); all reassigned to level C. Accuracy highest for level D (94.3%), with marked over-triage of low and intermediate risk presentations.
evidence.quote: Emergency under-triage occurred in 23 of 410 level D trials (5.6%), and all under-triaged emergencies were reassigned to level C urgency.

evidence.title: Persona-Grounded Safety Evaluation of AI Companions in Multi-Turn Conversations
evidence.outcome: Companion chatbot responses to high-risk personas in multi-turn scenarios (self-harm, disordered eating, violent fantasy)
evidence.effect: Replika frequently mirrored or normalized unsafe content such as self-harm, disordered eating, and violent-fantasy narratives across 1,674 dialogue pairs in 25 high-risk scenarios.
evidence.quote: Results show that Replika exhibits a narrow emotional range dominated by curiosity and care, while frequently mirroring or normalizing unsafe content such as self-harm, disordered eating, and violent-fantasy narratives.

evidence.title: Lost in Delusion: Examining LLM Safety Under User Delusions and Distress
evidence.outcome: Timely escalation of safety-critical distress in multi-turn conversations
evidence.effect: Safety interventions were suppressed by up to 4.5x under delusional framing despite comparable distress detection.
evidence.quote: This reveals a recognition-intervention gap: models detect distress at comparable rates regardless of framing, yet sharply fail to act on it once distress is embedded in delusion, with safety interventions suppressed by up to 4.5x.

evidence.title: ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments
evidence.outcome: Missed red flag rate and diagnostic accuracy in adversarial simulated multi-turn encounters
evidence.effect: Trained agent improved diagnostic accuracy under adversarial conditions (88.0% vs. 81.0%) and reduced missed red flag rates by 31% relative to the base model.
evidence.quote: On held-out evaluations, the ResidencyRL agent improves diagnostic accuracy by 7.0% under adversarial conditions (88.0% vs. 81.0%) and reduces missed red flag rates by 31%, demonstrating rigorous mitigation of premature closure.

evidence.title: How LLMs Respond to Escalating Delusions: Four Longitudinal Trajectories of Model Behavior
evidence.outcome: Recognition and appropriate response to escalating psychosis across a 30-day multi-turn simulated conversation
evidence.effect: Four trajectories found: premature medicalization, recognition without safeguarding, delayed and unstable recognition, and delusion co-construction (Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, DeepSeek-V3, Claude Sonnet 4). Most models failed to recognize or safeguard reliably.
evidence.quote: Across model generations and vendors, we identified four response trajectories: (1) premature medicalization and disengagement (Claude Haiku 4.5); (2) recognition without safeguarding, marked by LLM self-sufficiency in offering help (GPT Instant/Thinking); (3) delayed and unstable recognition, marked by late, non-progressive conceptualization (Claude Opus 3/4/4.1, Claude Haiku 3.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 3.1 Pro); and (4) delusion co-construction through active engagement with delusional content (Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, DeepSeek-V3, Claude Sonnet 4).

evidence.title: Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation: A Conversational Benchmark for Safe Stroke Care in Japanese Using Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Critical mistakes in emergency stroke management by LLMs in multi-turn conversations
evidence.effect: Eleven models made 17 critical mistakes, including failure to confirm labs or blood glucose before t-PA, surgery before airway stabilization, omission of cervical vascular evaluation, and t-PA outside indication.
evidence.quote: Eleven models made 17 critical mistakes, including failure to confirm laboratory results or blood glucose before t-PA, surgery before airway stabilization, omission of cervical vascular evaluation, and t-PA outside its indication.

evidence.title: Clinician-Grounded Quality Assurance for AI-Assisted Psychiatric Intake
evidence.outcome: Characterization of identified safety concerns by LLM vs clinician intake interviewers in simulated patient interviews
evidence.effect: LLM characterized identified safety concerns less often than clinicians (33.3% vs. 66.7%).
evidence.quote: the LLM recovered more of the clinically relevant items embedded in the patient vignettes (88.0% vs. 38.9%), but made more clinical inferences not based on the interview (56.8% vs. 27.8%), and characterized identified safety concerns less often (33.3% vs. 66.7%)

evidence.title: AI-Powered Triage of Suicidal Ideation in Adolescents: A Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Models Using Synthetic Clinical Vignettes
evidence.outcome: Recognition of safety-critical suicide risk and appropriateness of action plans in vignettes
evidence.effect: Consistent adherence to basic safety protocols such as emergency evaluation for high-risk cases, but pervasive critical failures: omitted lethal means inquiry, no protective factors, inappropriate reassurance.
evidence.quote: Qualitative thematic analysis of the action plans identified consistent adherence to basic safety protocols (e.g., recommending emergency evaluation for high-risk cases).

evidence.title: Evaluating the Clinical Safety of LLMs in Response to High-Risk Mental Health Disclosures
evidence.outcome: LLM recognition of and safe response to simulated crisis-level mental health disclosures
evidence.effect: Claude outperformed all others; Grok 3, ChatGPT, and LLAMA underperformed across multiple domains; few models consistently provided specific resources or kept the conversation open. No numeric results in the abstract.
evidence.quote: These findings suggest that while LLMs show potential for emotionally attuned communication, none currently meet satisfactory clinical standards for crisis response.

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Depression Assessment: Simulating Patients and Clinicians in MADRS Administration
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM-estimated suicidality severity ratings in simulated MADRS assessments
evidence.effect: 30% of maximum suicide risk ratings were underestimated by two or more severity levels; most configurations underestimated severe presentations.
evidence.quote: Item-level analysis revealed excellent accuracy for concrete symptoms (Inner Tension r=0.91, Reduced Sleep r=0.88) but with concerning underestimation of severe suicidality: 30% of maximum suicide risk ratings were underestimated by two or more severity levels.

evidence.title: Clinical Safety of Large Language Models in Oral Cancer–Related Patient Communication: A Longitudinal Study
evidence.outcome: Referral safety (binary) of LLM responses to oral cancer patient scenarios
evidence.effect: Referral-safe responses in 90.0% of Gemini and 92.1% of Grok outputs (p = 0.536), so roughly 8-10% of responses were not referral-safe.
evidence.quote: Referral-safe responses were observed in 90.0% of Gemini and 92.1% of Grok outputs (p = 0.536).

evidence.title: Effect of Prompt Structure on Large Language Model-Recommended Triage Levels in Urologic Patient Messages
evidence.outcome: Missed urgent conditions and omission of critical warnings in triage of patient messages
evidence.effect: No unsafe undertriage or omission of critical warnings occurred in any arm (150 outputs).
evidence.quote: No unsafe undertriage or omission of critical warnings occurred in any arm.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM outputs (50 synthetic urologic patient messages x 3 prompt arms)

evidence.title: Persona system prompts reshape simulated clinical reasoning: a 2×2 factorial in-silico experiment decomposing time pressure and safety priority
evidence.outcome: Safety-critical sequencing and contraindication violations in simulated ED cases under time-pressure/lean prompts
evidence.effect: Violations occurred only in High×LEAN condition (8/56, 14.3% overall); all in trap cases, high severity (mean 2.75/3).
evidence.quote: Contraindication/sequence violations occurred only in the High×LEAN condition (8/56, 14.3% overall); all violations occurred in trap cases and were high severity (mean 2.75/3).

evidence.title: An independent supervisory safety agent improves reaction of large language models to suicidal ideation
evidence.outcome: Native LLM recognition of suicide risk in clinical vignettes (single-turn)
evidence.effect: Native LLM safeguards detected suicide risk in only 41 of 224 evaluations (18.3%); detection lower in ambiguous presentations.
evidence.quote: Native LLM safeguards frequently failed to detect suicide risk in this structured evaluation.

evidence.title: Medical errors in large language models revealed using 1,000 synthetic clinical transcripts
evidence.outcome: Triage safety for life- or sight-threatening emergencies in simulated headache consultations
evidence.effect: Models downgraded triage to self-management or routine follow-up in up to 54.8% of emergency cases (GPT-5-mini; 95% CI 40.5-69.0).
evidence.quote: For life- or sight-threatening emergencies, models inappropriately downgraded triage to self-management or routine follow-up in up to 54.8% cases (GPT-5-mini; 95% CIs: 40.5-69.0).

evidence.title: Bridging Artificial and Human Intelligence: Comparative Performance of AI Models and Neurologists in Stroke Recognition- A Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: Advising ED visit for suspected stroke posts, LLMs vs neurologists
evidence.effect: Neurologists advised ED visit in 58.5% vs ChatGPT 45% and Gemini 45% (p < 0.001); LLMs gave 'Unable to determine' in 11.5% (ChatGPT) and 14.5% (Gemini) vs 0% for neurologists.
evidence.quote: Neurologists were much more willing to advocate for visiting the ED (58.5%) than ChatGPT (45%) or Gemini (45%) (p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: Reddit AskDocs posts about possible stroke symptoms

evidence.title: MTS-Bench: A Manchester Triage System Benchmark for Language Model Triage Safety
evidence.outcome: Undertriage rate of emergency scenarios against Manchester Triage System priority levels
evidence.effect: GPT-5.1 undertriaged 44.2% (69/156), including 75.0% of Red and 73.4% of Orange prompts; both DR. INFO configurations undertriaged 11.5% (18/156).
evidence.quote: GPT-5.1 undertriaged 44.2% of prompts (69/156; 95% CI 36.7 to 52.1), including 75.0% of Red-priority and 73.4% of Orange-priority prompts.
evidence.sample_unit: prompts per system (39 cases x 4 permutations x with/without anchoring statement)

evidence.title: Conversational AI and Emerging Psychosis: A Simulation Study of Potentially Iatrogenic Response Patterns
evidence.outcome: Critical errors and safety failures in chatbot responses across escalating psychosis conversation turns
evidence.effect: 39 of 189 responses (20.6%) met critical error criteria; severity increased as psychotic symptoms escalated; no chatbot recommended for use in this scenario.
evidence.quote: A total of 39 responses (20.6%) met predefined criteria for critical errors, and severity ratings increased as psychotic symptoms escalated throughout the conversation.

evidence.title: Evaluating Five Generative AI Chatbots for Myocarditis-Related Public Health Consultation: A Multidimensional Assessment of Safety, Accuracy, Empathy, Reliability, Quality, and Readability
evidence.outcome: Under-triage of serious cardiopulmonary symptoms and ambiguous escalation advice in chatbot responses
evidence.effect: 21 safety-flagged responses; safe rates 90.4%–94.2%; mechanisms included under-triage of serious cardiopulmonary symptoms and ambiguous escalation advice; unsafe outputs occurred across all models.
evidence.quote: Qualitative analysis of 21 safety-flagged responses identified five recurrent mechanisms of potential unsafety: under-triage of serious cardiopulmonary symptoms, over-reassurance regarding vaccine-associated myocarditis, premature or insufficiently individualized exercise guidance, incomplete treatment framing, and ambiguous escalation advice.

evidence.title: Reducing Under-Triage Risk in Large Language Model Based Clinical Triage Using UMLS-CUI Augmentation
evidence.outcome: Baseline LLM recognition of emergency cases in triage vignettes
evidence.effect: Baseline emergency-case accuracy was 73.0% for GPT-4o-mini and 60.5% for MedGemma 27B, indicating missed emergencies.
evidence.quote: Emergency-case accuracy improved from 73.0% to 80.7% for GPT-4o-mini and from 60.5% to 68.5% for MedGemma 27B.

evidence.title: GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 responses to common migraine questions: a cross-sectional comparative study of accuracy, completeness, empathy, readability and safety
evidence.outcome: Safety scores of LLM responses to red-flag migraine questions (possible stroke or secondary headache)
evidence.effect: Among 25 red-flag questions, both models had high safety scores; no significant difference in safety after correction (overall safety adjusted p = 0.075).
evidence.quote: Among 25 red-flag questions, both models had high safety scores; only readability remained significantly different after correction.

evidence.title: Inconsistent and divergent large language model safety guidance during intraoperative crises: a guideline- anchored benchmark
evidence.outcome: Omission of communication and escalation safety actions during simulated intraoperative crises
evidence.effect: Omissions were highest for communication and escalation actions and varied nearly threefold across models under an identical prompt (24.6 to 72.6 percent).
evidence.quote: Omissions fell most on communication and escalation actions, where omission varied nearly threefold across models under an identical prompt (24.6 to 72.6 percent).
evidence.sample_unit: model runs (10 scenarios x 3 models x 3 runs)

evidence.title: Evaluating Safety-Critical Communication Behavior of Large Language Models Using Workflow-Embedded Multi-Agent Clinical Simulation
evidence.outcome: Safety-critical omissions in LLM ward deterioration escalation conversations
evidence.effect: Omissions persisted under both conditions (16.0% ISBAR vs 11.5% unstructured); ISBAR did not eliminate all failure modes.
evidence.quote: Structured ISBAR communication improves LLM escalation performance by constraining information flow and reducing hallucinated content, but does not eliminate all failure modes.

evidence.title: The Diagnostic and Triage Accuracy of the GPT-3 Artificial Intelligence Model
evidence.outcome: Correct triage of case vignettes including emergencies by GPT-3 versus physicians and lay people
evidence.effect: GPT-3 triaged 71% correct (95% CI, 57% to 82%), similar to lay individuals (74%) and significantly worse than physicians (91%; p<0.001).
evidence.quote: GPT-3 triaged (71% correct; 95% CI, 57% to 82%) similarly to lay individuals (74%; 95% CI, 73% to 75%; p=0.73); both were significantly worse than physicians (91%; 95% CI, 89% to 93%; p<0.001).

evidence.title: Assessment of ChatGPT in the preclinical management of ophthalmological emergencies – an analysis of ten fictional case vignettes
evidence.outcome: Triage accuracy and harm potential in emergency vignette responses
evidence.effect: Triage accuracy 87.2%; potential to inflict harm present in 32% of answers.
evidence.quote: However, an overall potential to inflict harm to users/patients was present in 32% of answers.

evidence.title: Quality of information and appropriateness of ChatGPT outputs for urology patients
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT responses for emergency urology cases
evidence.effect: Only 11.1% of emergency urology case responses were appropriate, versus 58.5% non-oncology and 52.6% oncology (p = 0.03).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT provided more appropriate responses for non-oncology conditions (58.5%) compared to oncology (52.6%) and emergency urology cases (11.1%) (p = 0.03).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence chatbot performance in triage of ophthalmic conditions
evidence.venue: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie
evidence.outcome: Correct triage urgency of ophthalmic vignettes by chatbots versus trainees
evidence.effect: Triage urgency appropriate in 38 (86%) trainees, 43 (98%) ChatGPT, 37 (84%) Bing Chat; Bing tended to overestimate urgency.
evidence.quote: Triage urgency was appropriate in 38 (86%), 43 (98%), and 37 (84%) cases for ophthalmology trainees, ChatGPT, and Bing Chat, correspondingly.

evidence.title: Complications Following Facelift and Neck Lift: Implementation and Assessment of Large Language Model and Artificial Intelligence (ChatGPT) Performance Across 16 Simulated Patient Presentations
evidence.outcome: Recognition of red-flag symptoms and appropriate disposition in simulated complications of varying acuity
evidence.effect: Red-flag symptoms identified with 73% accuracy; appropriate disposition in 56% of cases, with urgency overestimated in 44%.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT overestimated the urgency of indicated patient dispositions in 44% of cases, concerning for potential unnecessary increase in healthcare resource utilization.

evidence.title: Assessment of ChatGPT in the Prehospital Management of Ophthalmological Emergencies - An Analysis of 10 Fictional Case Vignettes
evidence.outcome: Triage accuracy and potential for harm of ChatGPT answers to ophthalmological emergency vignettes
evidence.effect: Triage accuracy 93.6%; most prehospital recommendations appropriate, but potential to inflict harm to users/patients present in 32% of answers.
evidence.quote: However, an overall potential to inflict harm to users/patients was present in 32% of answers.
evidence.sample_unit: ChatGPT answers (10 fictional vignettes entered 5 times each)

evidence.title: "ChatGPT, Can You Help Me Save My Child's Life?" - Diagnostic Accuracy and Supportive Capabilities to Lay Rescuers by ChatGPT in Prehospital Basic Life Support and Paediatric Advanced Life Support Cases - An In-silico Analysis
evidence.outcome: Emergency recognition and advice to call emergency services in paediatric emergency vignettes
evidence.effect: Both models recognized the emergency in the cases except septic shock and pulmonary embolism; reliably advised calling emergency services in only 12 of 22 cases (54%).
evidence.quote: However, ChatGPT/GPT-4 reliably advised to call emergency services only in 12 of 22 cases (54%), gave correct first aid instructions in 9 cases (45%) and incorrectly advised advanced life support techniques to parents in 3 of 22 cases (13.6%).
evidence.sample_unit: case vignettes (each run three times per model)

evidence.title: Safety of Large Language Models in Addressing Depression
evidence.outcome: Point at which chatbot recommended human support during simulated escalating suicide risk
evidence.effect: Referral occurred around the simulation mid-point; average initial referral at PHQ-9 score 12 and shutdown at 25; definitive shutdown mostly only at highest risk levels.
evidence.quote: Current generative AI-based conversational agents are slow to escalate mental health risk scenarios, postponing referral to a human to potentially dangerous levels.

evidence.title: The role of an artificial intelligence model in antiretroviral therapy counselling and advice for people living with HIV
evidence.outcome: Recognition of life-threatening scenarios such as abacavir hypersensitivity reaction
evidence.effect: ChatGPT recognized potentially life-threatening scenarios such as abacavir hypersensitivity reaction and gave appropriate advice.
evidence.quote: It recognized potentially life-threatening scenarios such as abacavir hypersensitivity reaction and gave appropriate advice.

evidence.title: ChatGPT is not ready yet for use in providing mental health assessment and interventions
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness and safety of ChatGPT recommendations across simulated mental health cases of rising complexity
evidence.effect: Case A recommendations were relatively appropriate but non-specific. In more complex cases B and C, recommendations became inappropriate, even dangerous.
evidence.quote: However, as complexity of clinical cases increased (cases B and C), the information and recommendations generated by ChatGPT became inappropriate, even dangerous; and the limitations of the program became more glaring.

evidence.title: Patients with floaters: Answers from virtual assistants and large language models
evidence.outcome: Whether responses conveyed urgency or emergency nature of floaters/retinal detachment
evidence.effect: No tool mentioned the urgency or emergency nature of floaters; all missed the urgency of diagnosing retinal detachment.
evidence.quote: There is no mention of the urgency or emergency nature of floaters.
evidence.sample_unit: questions posed to each of four tools

evidence.title: Exploring Diagnostic Precision and Triage Proficiency: A Comparative Study of GPT-4 and Bard in Addressing Common Ophthalmic Complaints
evidence.outcome: Appropriate triage/urgency recommendations for simulated ophthalmic complaints across urgency levels
evidence.effect: Appropriate triage 90.0% overall; GPT-4 96.3% vs Bard 83.8% (p=0.008); potential harm 6.3% GPT-4 vs 20.0% Bard (p=0.010).
evidence.quote: GPT-4 performed better than Bard for appropriate triage recommendations (96.3% vs. 83.8%; p = 0.008), grader satisfaction for patient use (81.3% vs. 55.0%; p < 0.001), and lower potential harm rates (6.3% vs. 20.0%; p = 0.010).

evidence.title: Evaluation of the safety, accuracy, and helpfulness of the GPT-4.0 Large Language Model in neurosurgery
evidence.venue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
evidence.outcome: Missed red flag symptoms in GPT-4.0 neurosurgical responses
evidence.effect: "Red flag" symptoms were missed 7.1% of the time; depth of clinical responses varied (3.7 ± 0.6).
evidence.quote: The depth of clinical responses varied (3.7 ± 0.6), and "red flag" symptoms were missed 7.1 % of the time.

evidence.title: Evaluating generative AI responses to real-world drug-related questions
evidence.outcome: Recognition of suicidal ideation and emergency escalation in AI responses to real forum questions
evidence.effect: Clinicians rated responses as high quality, but instances of dangerous disinformation were found, including disregard for suicidal ideation, incorrect emergency helplines, and endorsement of home detox.
evidence.quote: While clinicians rated the AI-generated responses as high quality, we discovered instances of dangerous disinformation, including disregard for suicidal ideation, incorrect emergency helplines, and endorsement of home detox.

evidence.title: The diagnostic and triage accuracy of the GPT-3 artificial intelligence model: an observational study
evidence.outcome: Recognition and appropriate triage of emergent cases by GPT-3
evidence.effect: GPT-3 triaged 70% correct (34/48) versus 91% for physicians; GPT-3 deprioritised truly emergent cases in seven instances.
evidence.quote: For triage error analysis, GPT-3 deprioritised truly emergent cases in seven instances.

evidence.title: Digesting Digital Health: A Study of Appropriateness and Readability of ChatGPT-Generated Gastroenterological Information
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT responses to gastrointestinal emergency questions
evidence.effect: None of ChatGPT's responses to questions related to gastrointestinal emergencies were designated appropriate.
evidence.quote: Notably, none of ChatGPT's responses to questions related to gastrointestinal emergencies were designated appropriate.

evidence.title: Accuracy of Prospective Assessments of 4 Large Language Model Chatbot Responses to Patient Questions About Emergency Care: Experimental Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Recognition and appropriate advice for emergency conditions; dangerous information in chatbot responses
evidence.effect: Chatbots contained dangerous information in 5% to 35% of responses; accuracy and completeness about 50%; information on when to seek urgent care frequently incomplete and inaccurate.
evidence.quote: Chatbots contained dangerous information in 5% to 35% of responses, with no statistical difference between chatbots on this metric (P=.24).
evidence.sample_unit: expert assessments (5 EM faculty x 10 questions x 8 domains per chatbot; 400 per chatbot)

evidence.title: "Comparative analysis of large language models against the NHS 111 online triaging for emergency ophthalmology"
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM responses to ophthalmology emergency triage scenarios versus NHS 111
evidence.effect: Score of ≥1 graded as "Good" was achieved by 93% of all LLM responses; very similar results on both prompts.
evidence.quote: The score of ≥1 graded as "Good" was achieved by 93% responses of all LLMs.

evidence.title: Detecting emergencies in patient portal messages using large language models and knowledge graph-based retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Recognition of emergencies in patient messages by LLM without retrieval
evidence.effect: Prompt-only model sensitivity 0.73 [0.57, 0.86], missing about a quarter of emergency messages; an emergency drug-interaction message was missed by three of four models.
evidence.quote: The prompt-only model, while achieving an accuracy of 0.91 [0.89, 0.93], showed limitations in sensitivity (0.73 [0.5, 0.86]) and precision (0.27 [0.19, 0.35]), indicating a lower capability to correctly identify emergency messages and a higher rate of false positives.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of generative AI-large language models' recognition of veteran suicide risk: a comparison with human mental health providers using a risk stratification model
evidence.outcome: LLM recognition of acute suicide risk in vignettes versus mental health providers
evidence.effect: GAI-LLMs rated the most acute case as less acute than MHCPs and the least acute case as more acute; ChatGPT-3.5 gave lower acute risk ratings than ChatGPT-4o and Gemini.
evidence.quote: GAI-LLMs' assessments showed discrepancies with MHCPs, particularly rating the most acute case as less acute and the least acute case as more acute.

evidence.title: Opportunities and risks of artificial intelligence in patient portal messaging in primary care
evidence.outcome: AI drafts failing to escalate urgent conditions (blood clot, DKA) in patient messages
evidence.effect: AI drafts for blood clot risk and DKA risk omitted urgent escalation; these were missed by 13 (65%) and 15 (75%) physicians respectively.
evidence.quote: The AI draft does not address the risk of diabetic ketoacidosis which requires urgent intervention.

evidence.title: Are clinical improvements in large language models a reality? Longitudinal comparisons of ChatGPT models and DeepSeek-R1 for psychiatric assessments and interventions
evidence.venue: The International journal of social psychiatry
evidence.outcome: Recognition of suicidality and risk stratification across psychiatric vignettes
evidence.effect: Clinical reasoning worsened with case complexity, especially for suicidality safeguards and risk stratification, in ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-4.5 and DeepSeek-R1.
evidence.quote: Nevertheless, consistent with past findings, clinical reasoning worsened as case complexity increased; this was especially apparent for suicidality safeguards and risk stratification.

evidence.title: Is Readability a Proxy for Reliability? A Qualitative Evaluation of ChatGPT-4.0 in Orthopaedic Trauma Communication
evidence.venue: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
evidence.outcome: Safety and accuracy of ChatGPT-4.0 responses to orthopaedic emergency questions rated by surgeons
evidence.effect: Accuracy and safety scores varied considerably; some responses rated poor or dangerous; safety ICC 0.68.
evidence.quote: Accuracy and safety scores varied considerably among responses, with the highest inter-rater agreement in clinical appropriateness (ICC = 0.81) and the lowest in safety assessments (ICC = 0.68).
evidence.sample_unit: patient FAQ questions (responses rated by 3 surgeons)

evidence.title: Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
evidence.outcome: Recognition and escalation of suicidal crisis in escalating simulated chatbot scenarios
evidence.effect: No agent gave an adequate response; 48.28% were inadequate. Common errors included failure to provide emergency contact information and poor contextual understanding.
evidence.quote: Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding.

evidence.title: The impact of prompting on ChatGPT's adherence to status epilepticus treatment guidelines
evidence.outcome: Recognition of emergency management steps and context in status epilepticus scenario
evidence.effect: Missed that the patient was already intubated in 25% of 4th-prompt responses; rarely recommended neurological assessment and side positioning.
evidence.quote: In the fourth prompt, it missed the fact that the described patient was already intubated.

evidence.title: The Performance of Artificial Intelligence in Providing Real-Time Aid in Emergency Dental Trauma: A Clinical Validation Study
evidence.venue: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology
evidence.outcome: Time-critical safety flag (accurate immediate action and contraindication advice) in emergency dental avulsion responses
evidence.effect: Safety flag present in 81% and 89% of cases across two sessions (p = 0.009), leaving roughly one in eight potentially unsafe situations.
evidence.quote: The safety flag was present in 81% and 89% of cases (χ<sup>2</sup> = 6.73, p = 0.009), with one in eight potentially unsafe situations.
evidence.sample_unit: chatbot responses (78 avulsion vignettes x 2 sessions)

evidence.title: Utility and Safety of Artificial Intelligence for Patient-Initiated Contact After Functional Rhinoplasty
evidence.outcome: Expert approval of chatbot responses to red flag postoperative complication questions
evidence.effect: Experts unanimously approved ChatGPT responses 96% of the time overall and 100% for the 6 Red Flag Questions.
evidence.quote: Experts unanimously approved ChatGPT responses (mean EOQ = 1) 96% of the time, and 100% for Red Flag Questions.

evidence.title: Evaluation of the effectiveness of the ChatGPT artificial intelligence application in the diagnosis of spontaneous pneumothorax on chest radiograph interpretation
evidence.outcome: Missed detection of a potentially life-threatening condition (small pneumothorax)
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 70.9% overall; small pneumothorax AUC 0.439 (below chance), with risk of under-triaging.
evidence.quote: Any use of ChatGPT in diagnostic workflows should be approached with caution, as unverified outputs may lead to inappropriate interventions or under-triaging.

evidence.title: Cautionary lessons from real-world testing of GPT-4.1 AI for pediatric foreign body aspiration
evidence.venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: Detection of confirmed bronchial foreign body aspiration cases (missed emergencies) by GPT-4.1
evidence.effect: Detected only 4 of 12 confirmed bronchial-aspiration cases and missed all left-bronchus aspirations; recall 19.0%, precision 23.3%, accuracy 62.3%.
evidence.quote: While it correctly identified 34 of 46 cases without aspiration, it detected only 4 of 12 confirmed bronchial-aspiration cases and missed all left-bronchus aspirations.

evidence.title: AI-assisted PEG aftercare education for older adults: clinician-informed chatbot design (PEGAssist)
evidence.outcome: Recognition of complication red flags and escalation pathways in chatbot responses to PEG questions
evidence.effect: Responses consistently highlighted clear red-flag signs (infection, tube dislodgement, persistent pain) and specified escalation pathways (self-care, 24-48 h contact, urgent evaluation); no unsafe recommendations identified.
evidence.quote: Performance was strongest in complication management, where responses consistently highlighted clear red-flag signs (e.g., infection, tube dislodgement, and persistent pain) and specified escalation pathways (self-care, 24-48 h contact, urgent evaluation).
evidence.sample_unit: chatbot responses to curated PEG aftercare questions

evidence.title: Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence for Patient Self-Triage: Comparison of General-Purpose AI Platforms With the NHS 111 Online Symptom Checker in the United Kingdom
evidence.outcome: Missed or delayed escalation of emergencies by conversational AI in simulated scenarios
evidence.effect: Both ChatGPT GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Flash correctly identified all five emergency cases, while NHS 111 under-triaged one.
evidence.quote: Both AI platforms correctly identified all emergency cases; NHS 111 under-triaged one acute emergency.

evidence.title: AI vs. MD: Benchmarking ChatGPT and Gemini for Complex Wound Management
evidence.outcome: Recognition of critical red flags such as ischemia requiring urgent vascular assessment
evidence.effect: Both LLMs demonstrated high proficiency in recognizing critical red flags such as signs of ischemia requiring urgent vascular assessment.
evidence.quote: Both LLMs demonstrated high proficiency in identifying the etiology of vascular lesions and recognizing critical "red flags," such as signs of ischemia requiring urgent vascular assessment.

evidence.title: Comparative analysis of six large language models in perioperative decision support for geriatric patients with multimorbidity: a three-dimensional evaluation framework
evidence.outcome: Addressing extreme-event or emergency protocols (aortic rupture management) in perioperative recommendations
evidence.effect: Safety redundancy was a universal failure: no model addressed extreme-event protocols such as aortic rupture management.
evidence.quote: Safety redundancy emerged as a universal failure—no model addressed extreme-event protocols (aortic rupture management).
evidence.sample_unit: simulated clinical case (scored outputs from six LLMs)

evidence.title: Large Language Models Triage of Retina Patient Emergency Telephone Calls: A Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM chatbot diagnosis and triage/follow-up recommendations for simulated retina emergency calls versus humans
evidence.effect: Humans more accurate than chatbots in diagnosis (95% vs 76.7%, P<.01) and follow-up (85% vs 70%, P=.03); ChatGPT and Claude noninferior, Gemini (50%) and Meta (46.7%) worse in follow-up.
evidence.quote: Human graders were significantly more accurate than chatbots in diagnosis (95% vs 76.7%, respectively; P < .01) and follow-up recommendations (85% vs 70%, respectively; P = .03).

evidence.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models in the Diagnosis, Urgency Triage, and Initial Management of Ophthalmic Emergencies
evidence.outcome: Urgency recognition and red flag identification scores of LLMs on ophthalmic emergency vignettes
evidence.effect: Overall scores 6.88 (ChatGPT), 7.03 (Gemini), 6.93 (Claude) of 8; no significant differences in urgency triage or red flag recognition; diagnostic errors and suboptimal management noted.
evidence.quote: Additional comparison across diagnostic scores, urgency triage, red flag recognition, and management scores yielded no significant differences between any of the LLMs.

evidence.title: ChatGPT Health performance in a structured test of triage recommendations
evidence.outcome: Emergency recognition and escalation by consumer chatbot across vignettes
evidence.effect: Undertriaged 52% of gold-standard emergencies, directing DKA or impending respiratory failure to 24-48 h evaluation instead of the ED; classical emergencies such as stroke and anaphylaxis were triaged correctly.
evidence.quote: Among gold-standard emergencies, the system undertriaged 52% of cases, directing patients with diabetic ketoacidosis or impending respiratory failure to 24-48 h evaluation rather than the emergency department, while correctly triaging classical emergencies such as stroke and anaphylaxis.

evidence.title: Simulated evaluation of large language model stepwise diagnostic reasoning with real-world chest pain encounters and Bayesian networks
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: emergent diagnosis recognition
evidence.effect: No-category prompt: 19 TP, 198 FN; sensitivity 8.8% (5.7–13.3), specificity 94.7% (91.4–96.8).
evidence.quote: Removing diagnostic category constraints further increased specificity (94.7%, 95% CI 91.4–96.8) with minimal sensitivity (8.8%, 95% CI 5.7–13.3).

evidence.title: Patient perspective on large-language model responses to questions about Moyamoya
evidence.outcome: Physician-rated failure of LLM answers to address urgent symptoms warranting referral
evidence.effect: Physicians reported answers failed to address urgent symptoms warranting referral to higher levels of care (ChatGPT 70.0%, Gemini 70.0%).
evidence.quote: Physicians evaluating the same LLM outputs reported the answers failed to address recent advances and research within the field (ChatGPT 57.5%, Gemini 62.5%) and failed to address urgent symptoms warranting referral to higher levels of care (ChatGPT 70.0%, Gemini 70.0%).
evidence.sample_unit: community respondent survey sets (27 ChatGPT, 20 Gemini)

evidence.title: Structural error asymmetry and harm-weighted analysis of ChatGPT versus ICU Physicians in acid-base interpretation: a prospective observational study
evidence.outcome: False reassurance: mixed acid-base disorders misclassified as normal by ChatGPT
evidence.effect: ChatGPT classified 16.7% of mixed cases as normal; ICU physicians produced no false-normal classifications.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT uniquely classified 16.7% of mixed cases as normal (false reassurance), whereas ICU physicians produced no false-normal classifications.
evidence.sample_unit: consecutive ICU patients' arterial blood gas interpretations

evidence.title: Multi-modal large language models for paediatric tele-ophthalmology: A blinded real-world evaluation of diagnostic accuracy and safety
evidence.outcome: Rate of major harmful responses by model in tele-consultation cases
evidence.effect: Major harmful responses: Grok 4.1 4%, GPT 5.1 Thinking 8%, Gemini 2.5 Pro 10%, GPT-4o 16%.
evidence.quote: Regarding safety, advanced models exhibited markedly fewer major harmful responses (Grok 4.1: 4%; GPT 5.1 Thinking: 8%; Gemini 2.5 Pro: 10%) compared to GPT-4o (16%).

evidence.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence Algorithms in Challenging Diagnostic Cases - Between Potential and Real Clinical Support
evidence.outcome: Whether platforms recognized a rare lymphoma from early and advanced case data
evidence.effect: Six of eight platforms gave valid differentials; early-stage data mainly yielded infectious diagnoses; at advanced stage only Doctronic and Symptomate explicitly included lymphoma.
evidence.quote: Early-stage data mainly generated infectious diagnoses like peritonsillar abscess.

evidence.title: Intelligent virtual agents in psychotherapy: a safety evaluation across high-risk mental health scenarios
evidence.outcome: Rated safety of chatbot responses in suicidality and substance-use scenarios, including risk recognition and crisis referral
evidence.effect: Problematic responses in 29% of conversations, 12.5% highly critical; inadequate risk recognition and insufficient referral to crisis resources, especially underage alcohol and suicide-related inquiries.
evidence.quote: However, problematic responses occurred in 29% of conversations, with 12.5% rated as highly critical.

evidence.title: Safety Audit of a Large Language Model for Lay Self-Triage Using Japanese Symptom Vignettes: Persistent Red-Flag Under-Triage Despite Improved Reproducibility Under Near-Deterministic Decoding
evidence.outcome: Primary-action under-triage of red-flag emergency vignettes
evidence.effect: Hard under-triage of primary action in red-flag slice was 100.0% for both prompts at T=0, 100.0% P1 and 99.7% P2 stochastic, 100.0% under schema.
evidence.quote: Under near-deterministic decoding, both P1 and P2 produced hard under-triage in 100.0% of red-flag outputs.

evidence.title: Open-Source Large Language Models Distilled DeepSeek-R1 Pose Challenges for On-Premises Clinical Deployment in Medical Diagnosis: A Comparative Study of Performance
evidence.outcome: Recognition of red-flag (serious) findings in incorrect diagnostic cases
evidence.effect: Red-flag recognition failure was one of three universally prevalent error modes in distilled models' incorrect cases (qualitative; no counts reported).
evidence.quote: Qualitative analysis of the chain-of-thought outputs in incorrect cases revealed three universally prevalent error modes across distilled models: Reasoning drift, Red-Flag recognition failure, and diagnostic priority inversion.

evidence.title: Evaluating the clinical safety of large language models in oral cancer-related patient communication: a repeated-prompt observational study
evidence.outcome: Referral safety (recommending professional consultation) in suspected oral cancer scenarios
evidence.effect: Overall referral safety high (Gemini 90.0%; Grok 92.1%); Gemini failed to recommend professional consultation in two high-risk suspected malignancy scenarios, Grok consistently referred.
evidence.quote: Overall referral safety was high (Gemini: 90.0%; Grok: 92.1%), although the Gemini model failed to recommend professional consultation in two high-risk scenarios involving suspected malignancy.

evidence.title: Evaluating a Consumer LLM for Suicide Risk Response Calibration: A Pilot Study
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
evidence.outcome: Recognition and escalation of suicide risk across vignette risk levels
evidence.effect: Safety escalation elements (risk acknowledgment, crisis resources) increased with risk level, approximating clinical triage, but the model failed to recognize implicit suicidality in an ambiguous ideation vignette.
evidence.quote: Notably, the model failed to recognize implicit suicidality in an ambiguous ideation vignette.

evidence.title: Persona Routing Associated With Fewer Safety and Monotonicity Violations in Simulated Emergency Large Language Model (LLM) Reasoning
evidence.outcome: Under-triage and omitted escalation actions for deteriorated emergency vignettes
evidence.effect: Lean persona had contraindication/sequence violations in 8/56 (14.3%); monotonicity violations dominated by under-triage of Worse vignettes below minimum admission level.
evidence.quote: Violations were dominated by under-triage patterns in which the Worse vignette received a plan below the minimum admission level implied by red-flag features, often accompanied by missing escalation actions.
evidence.sample_unit: scenario-level runs (28 synthetic emergency vignettes x 2 replicates); 16 Base/Worse counterfactual comparisons per strategy

evidence.title: Prompt Framing Modulates Safety in Shoulder and Elbow Red-Flag Vignettes: A Large Language Model Study
evidence.outcome: Safety-critical under-triage of red-flag shoulder/elbow vignettes by LLM
evidence.effect: Under-triage in 19 of 72 red-flag responses (26.4%); urgency correctly recognized in 53 (73.6%); patient-oriented prompts 10/24 (41.7%).
evidence.quote: Across the 72 prompt-specific responses derived from the 24 red-flag vignettes (24 vignettes × 3 prompt conditions), correct urgency classification was observed in 53 responses (73.6%), whereas safety-critical under-triage occurred in 19 responses (26.4%).
evidence.sample_unit: model responses (80 vignettes x 3 prompt types)

evidence.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models in Infectious Disease Decision-Making: From Examination to Clinical Practice
evidence.outcome: Recognition of high-risk clinical scenario (invasive pulmonary aspergillosis after influenza)
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1 and Grok 3 omitted invasive pulmonary aspergillosis from top three differentials; Grok 3 advised against antifungal treatment even after supporting evidence was provided.
evidence.quote: In this study, several models did not promptly recognize the elevated risk of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis in patients with influenza, leading to diagnostic errors and delayed antifungal recommendations.

evidence.title: FairGuard: Blockchain-Enforced Continuous Fairness Governance for Demographically Equitable LLM-Based Emergency Triage Decision Support
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
evidence.outcome: Under-triage of urgent patients by LLM triage support
evidence.effect: 50.9% of Urgent cases were misclassified as Non-Urgent, a conservative triage bias attributed to RAG corpus composition.
evidence.quote: Evaluated on the MIMIC-IV Full Emergency dataset (N=300-1,000), FairGuard achieves a gender ΔF1 of 0.020, well within threshold, while identifying RAG corpus composition as the root cause of conservative triage bias (50.9% Urgent → Non-Urgent misclassification), establishing that the observed bias is class-directional rather than demographically concentrated.

evidence.title: Triage safety of patient-facing AI chatbots for nipple discharge: A guideline-informed assessment of red-flag recognition and patient actionability
evidence.outcome: Red-flag recognition and potentially misleading/unsafe responses in simulated nipple discharge consultations
evidence.effect: Red-flag recognition 90.6% (1174/1296); 8/216 (3.7%) potentially misleading, none unsafe; 4 of 8 misleading responses were due to missed red-flag features.
evidence.quote: The overall red-flag recognition rate was 90.6 % (1174 of 1296; 95 % CI, 87.8 %-93.2 %), and the median response-level recognition rate was 100.0 % (interquartile range [IQR], 85.7 %-100.0 %).

evidence.title: Clinical Safety and Reliability of Large Language Models in Answering Hemorrhoid-Related Patient Questions: A Comparative Study of ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek
evidence.outcome: Recognition and communication of risk in high-risk hemorrhoid scenarios (alarm symptoms, bleeding, acute pain)
evidence.effect: No model gave harmful recommendations or guidance likely to cause substantial diagnostic delay; DeepSeek showed disproportionately urgent or alarmist language in some higher-risk scenarios; model divergence larger in clinically significant scenarios.
evidence.quote: No model generated directly harmful medical recommendations or explicit guidance likely to result in substantial diagnostic delay.

evidence.title: Assessing retina-specific ophthalmic counseling generated by an early public large language model across different levels of clinical urgency
evidence.outcome: Appropriate communication of urgency in LLM counseling for high-urgency retinal vignettes
evidence.effect: Counseling urgency did not differ from clinical urgency except for high-urgency AMD (p = 0.013) and high-urgency RD (p < 0.001); urgency differed between high/low DR (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Counseling urgency did not differ significantly from clinical urgency of all vignettes, except for the high-urgency AMD (p = 0.013) and high-urgency RD (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Accuracy and Readability of Generative Artificial Intelligence for Vascular Surgery Patients: A Specialist Based Evaluation Highlighting the Current Landscape of Safety Risks and Accessibility Gaps
evidence.venue: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
evidence.outcome: Urgency/escalation recommendations in ChatGPT answers to symptom questions
evidence.effect: Urgency varied significantly across sub-types of symptom related questions (p = .030), consistent with inconsistent escalation recommendations; misaligned urgency flagged as a safety concern.
evidence.quote: however, urgency varied significantly across sub-types of symptom related questions (p = .030), consistent with inconsistent escalation recommendations.

evidence.title: Iterative Multidisciplinary Development and Evaluation of a Patient-Facing Social Determinants of Health Chatbot Using Synthetic Data Simulation: Mixed Methods Study
evidence.outcome: Chatbot safety rating (recognition of health emergencies) across simulated cases, expert rater agreement
evidence.effect: Safety agreement=0.69% (95% CI 0.58-0.78), Fleiss κ=-0.04; domain focus agreement=0.51%, data completeness 0.59% (κ=0.18); other domains near ceiling (0.98-0.99).
evidence.quote: Lower performance was observed in domain focus and completeness (agreement=0.51%, 95% CI 0.40-0.61), completeness of data capture (agreement=0.59%, 95% CI 0.48-0.69; Fleiss κ=0.18), and safety (agreement=0.69%, 95% CI 0.58-0.78; Fleiss κ=-0.04), prompting targeted adaptations.

evidence.title: Patient-Facing AI System for Symptom Guidance Using Simulated Encounters and Physician Review: Analytical Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Urgent undertriage rate in simulated multiturn conversations versus physician panel ground truth
evidence.effect: Urgent undertriage in 28 of 406 cases (6.9%, 95% CI 4.6%-9.8%); did not meet prespecified criterion of less than 5%.
evidence.quote: Urgent undertriage was identified in 28 of 406 cases (6.9%, 95% CI 4.6%-9.8%), nonurgent undertriage in 56 of 305 (18.4%, 95% CI 14.2%-23.2%), and overtriage in 40 of 364 (11.0%, 95% CI 8.0%-14.7%).

evidence.title: Large language models for early childhood caries risk triage: A validation study using standardized pediatric dental vignettes
evidence.venue: Journal of the Indian Society of Pedodontics and Preventive Dentistry
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and false negative rate for identifying high-risk caries presentations needing immediate referral
evidence.effect: GPT-4 sensitivity 92.0% vs Gemini 2.5 Flash 80.0% (P = 0.032); false negative rate 8.0% vs 20.0%.
evidence.quote: GPT-4 achieved significantly higher sensitivity (92.0% vs. 80.0%; P = 0.032) and a lower FNR (8.0% vs. 20.0%), with superior readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 5.9 vs. 8.1), actionability (4.8 vs. 4.2), and cross-lingual consistency.

evidence.title: Subgroup Differences in Agreement Between an Algorithm Guided Large Language Model and Routine Emergency Department Triage
evidence.venue: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of LLM for urgent versus non-urgent ED triage classification
evidence.effect: Urgent/non-urgent AUC 0.768, sensitivity 0.630, specificity 0.906; lower-acuity discordance 9.8%, higher in older adults, diabetes, and trauma.
evidence.quote: For urgent/non-urgent classification, AUC was 0.768, sensitivity 0.630, specificity 0.906.

evidence.title: Can Large Language Models Identify When an Upper Extremity Problem Needs Nonurgent Attention? An Assessment of Multiple LLM Chatbots
evidence.venue: Inquiry : a journal of medical care organization, provision and financing
evidence.outcome: Recognition of urgent upper extremity emergencies (e.g., compartment syndrome) across initial and ongoing inquiry
evidence.effect: Compartment syndrome misidentified as nonurgent in 80% of scenarios on initial inquiry; four of five LLMs corrected on continued inquiry. Repeat at 24 months: 100% PPV, 95% NPV initially, 98% NPV after ongoing inquiry.
evidence.quote: Compartment syndrome was misidentified as nonurgent in 80% of scenarios on initial inquiry, although four of five LLMs corrected on continued inquiry.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses to scenarios (5 LLMs x scenarios, initial diagnosis)

evidence.title: OpenEvidence errs on the safe side in a structured test of triage recommendations
evidence.outcome: Emergency under-triage rate on clinician-authored triage vignettes
evidence.effect: OpenEvidence under-triaged 12.5% of emergency presentations versus 51.6% in the previously reported ChatGPT Health benchmark; objective data eliminated emergency under-triage (25% to 0%; p = 0.005).
evidence.quote: OpenEvidence under-triaged 12.5 % of emergency presentations versus 51.6 % in the previously reported ChatGPT Health benchmark, and over-triaged 68.0 % of nonurgent Home presentations (ChatGPT Health, 64.8 %).

evidence.title: Evaluating the Risks, Safety, and Reliability of Large Language Models in Military Medicine
evidence.outcome: Safety risks in LLM responses to critical care, overdose, and psychiatric vignettes
evidence.effect: Safety risks in 78 conversations (9.3%), most prominent in overdose, critical care, and psychiatric scenarios.
evidence.quote: Safety risks were most prominent in overdose, critical care, and psychiatric scenarios.

evidence.title: Safety, accuracy, empathy, information quality, and readability of publicly accessible LLM-based chatbots for traumatic brain injury and concussion questions: a cross-sectional comparative study
evidence.outcome: Potentially harmful chatbot responses, including under-triage of TBI and concussion situations
evidence.effect: 27 of 325 responses were classified as potentially harmful, mainly due to under-triage, overly reassuring imaging advice, premature return-to-activity or driving guidance, and insufficient pediatric caution; safe response proportions were 89.2 to 95.4%.
evidence.quote: However, 27 responses were classified as potentially harmful, mainly because of under-triage, overly reassuring advice regarding imaging findings, premature return-to-activity or driving guidance, and insufficient pediatric caution.

evidence.title: A comparative evaluation of generative AI chatbots for patient-oriented advice on painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy: safety, accuracy, guideline concordance, actionability, and readability
evidence.outcome: Chatbot urgent-care triage and delayed assessment risk in responses
evidence.effect: Every system generated at least one response with a plausible pathway to delayed assessment, inappropriate self-management, medication misuse, or preventable injury; urgent-care triage needs professional verification.
evidence.quote: Although no overall safety difference was detected, every system generated at least one response with a plausible pathway to inappropriate self-management, delayed assessment, medication or product misuse, or preventable injury.

evidence.title: The Psychogenic Machine: Simulating AI Psychosis, Delusion Reinforcement and Harm Enablement in Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Safety interventions offered across simulated multi-turn delusion scenarios
evidence.effect: Models offered safety interventions in roughly a third of applicable turns (mean SIS 0.37 ± 0.48); 51/128 (39.8%) of scenarios had no safety interventions offered.
evidence.quote: Models frequently enabled harmful user requests (mean HES of 0.69 $\pm$0.84) and offered safety interventions in only roughly a third of applicable turns (mean SIS of 0.37 $\pm$0.48).

evidence.title: Between Help and Harm: An Evaluation of Mental Health Crisis Handling by LLMs
evidence.outcome: LLM recognition of and appropriate response to indirect crisis signals
evidence.effect: Models were reliable for some explicit crises, but all struggled with indirect signals, default replies, and context misalignment.
evidence.quote: All models struggle with indirect signals, default replies, and context misalignment.

evidence.title: An AI-Based Behavioral Health Safety Filter and Dataset for Identifying Mental Health Crises in Text-Based Conversations
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of general content moderation guardrails for specific mental health crisis types
evidence.effect: NeMo and OpenAI Omni Moderation showed inconsistent performance across crisis types, with sensitivity below 0.10 for some categories, meaning missed crises.
evidence.quote: NVIDIA NeMo and OpenAI Omni Moderation Latest exhibited inconsistent performance across specific crisis types, with sensitivity for some categories falling below 0.10.
evidence.sample_unit: messages (1,800 simulated plus 794 Aegis mental health-related)

evidence.title: PediatricAnxietyBench: Evaluating Large Language Model Safety Under Parental Anxiety and Pressure in Pediatric Consultations
evidence.outcome: Emergency recognition and safety under adversarial parental pressure in pediatric queries
evidence.effect: Emergency recognition was absent; adversarial queries reduced safety by 8% (p=0.03), urgency causing largest drop (-1.40); critical failures 4.8% (70B) vs 12.0% (8B).
evidence.quote: Hedging strongly correlated with safety (r=0.68, p<0.001), while emergency recognition was absent.

evidence.title: A Women's Health Benchmark for Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: LLM failure on missed urgency indicators in women's health queries
evidence.effect: Models universally struggle with missed urgency indicators; overall failure rate approximately 60% across the benchmark.
evidence.quote: Notably, models universally struggle with "missed urgency" indicators, while newer models like GPT-5 show significant improvements in avoiding inappropriate recommendations.

evidence.title: Evaluation format, not model capability, drives triage failure in the assessment of consumer health AI
evidence.outcome: Emergency recognition and escalation by consumer LLM chatbots across triage scenarios
evidence.effect: DKA was triaged correctly in 100% of trials across all models and conditions. Forced-choice format registered under-triage (0-24% for three models) although free text recommended emergency care in 100%.
evidence.quote: The forced A/B/C/D format was the dominant failure mechanism: three models scored 0--24% with forced choice but 100% with free text (all $p < 10^{-8}$), consistently recommending emergency care in their own words while the forced-choice format registered under-triage.

evidence.title: The Validity Gap in Health AI Evaluation: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Benchmark Composition
evidence.outcome: Representation of safety-critical scenarios in benchmarks
evidence.effect: Suicide/self-harm queries comprised <0.7% of the corpus; safety-critical scenarios effectively absent.
evidence.quote: Safety-critical scenarios were effectively absent: suicide/self-harm queries comprised <0.7% of the corpus and chronic disease management only 5.5%.

evidence.title: Disentangling Prompt Element Level Risk Factors for Hallucinations and Omissions in Mental Health LLM Responses
evidence.outcome: Omission of safety-critical guidance in crisis and suicidal ideation prompts
evidence.effect: Omissions occurred in 13.2% of responses, concentrated in crisis and suicidal ideation prompts; hallucinations in 6.5%.
evidence.quote: Hallucinations occurred in 6.5% of responses and omissions in 13.2%, with omissions concentrated in crisis and suicidal ideation prompts.

evidence.title: Trivial Prompt Reframing Bypasses Safety Guardrails in Googleś MedGemma-4B
evidence.outcome: Model advising that emergency care can be skipped under attack framings
evidence.effect: Emergency-deferral guardrail strong at 4.7% ASR, but the authority framing was the only attack that breached it.
evidence.quote: the drug-interaction guardrail is nearly absent (83.2% ASR) while the emergency-deferral guardrail is strong (4.7%) -- and the authority framing is the only attack that breaches it.

evidence.title: PatientAgentBench: A Benchmark Framework for Evaluating Patient-Facing Health AI Agents
evidence.outcome: Omitted crisis resources in emergency scenarios during multi-turn agent conversations
evidence.effect: Frontier models fail on only 1-3% of cases, from unverified tool outputs and omitted crisis resources in an emergency.
evidence.quote: Clinical safety and workflow accuracy follow the same pattern: the weakest models fail often, fabricating unexecuted actions, while frontier models fail on only 1-3% of cases, from unverified tool outputs and omitted crisis resources in an emergency.

evidence.title: When Vocabulary Comprehension Fails Clinical Reasoning: Evaluating Therapy Bots' Safety Risks for Generation Alpha
evidence.outcome: Clinical risk calibration and crisis recognition in multi-turn Gen Alpha mental health conversations
evidence.effect: Models understand 76-82% of vocabulary but correctly calibrate only 64-72% of clinical risk; 34% baseline miss rate; three or more failure patterns yield 94% miss rates.
evidence.quote: Across evaluations of LLM architectures underlying therapy apps and general chatbots - Claude, GPT-4o, Llama-3.1 - models understand 76-82% of vocabulary but correctly calibrate only 64-72% of clinical risk, creating a 10-14 percentage point (pp) vocabulary-comprehension gap (p<.001, d>0.48) absent in human therapists (3pp, p=.22).

evidence.title: K-Bench: a clinically calibrated benchmark for evaluating large language models in high-risk mental health conversations
evidence.outcome: Risk exploration and supportive conversation in multi-turn high-risk mental health vignettes
evidence.effect: Leading models had combined-risk scores above 95, while risk exploration varied substantially among lower-performing configurations.
evidence.quote: Leading models combined strong supportive conversation with combined-risk scores above 95, whereas risk exploration exposed substantial variation among lower-performing configurations.

evidence.title: Vertical Model Paradox: Systemic Ethical Blind Spots in Domain-Specific Medical AI
evidence.outcome: Model pass rates on ethical stress prompts, including emergency fail-safes and refusal of risky procedures
evidence.effect: Severe vulnerabilities: 47.62% pass rate for clinical traceability of medical records and 52.38% for safely refusing high-risk physical therapy procedures, consistently lacking emergency fail-safes.
evidence.quote: Notably, models exhibited severe vulnerabilities in maintaining clinical traceability for medical records (pass rate 47.62%) and safely refusing high-risk physical therapy procedures (52.38%), consistently lacking emergency fail-safes and upfront regulatory disclaimers.

evidence.title: mpathic Psychologist-led AI Clinical Tests Eating Disorders Benchmark (mPACT-ED-v1.0)
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness of LLM responses to multi-turn disordered eating conversations, including risk-responsiveness, scored by clinicians
evidence.effect: Severity-weighted mPACT-ED composite scores ranged from 7.12 (Claude) to 6.22 (Grok 4.1) on a 0-10 scale, a gap of about 0.90 points.
evidence.quote: Across all evaluated conversations, models varied in their overall severity-weighted mPACT-ED scores with ranges between 7.12 (Claude) and 6.22 (Grok 4.1), representing a gap of approximately 0.90 points between the highest and lowest performers.

evidence.title: Evaluating and Enhancing an AI Mental Health Guide in High-Risk Mental Health Contexts
evidence.outcome: Safety accuracy on adversarial mental health prompts (mania, delusions, crisis markers) before and after DPO alignment
evidence.effect: Safety accuracy rose by up to 18.4 percentage points after alignment; the best TalkAI variant reached 81.4%, still below proprietary frontier models.
evidence.quote: Following alignment, safety accuracy increased by up to 18.4 percentage points, with the most optimized TalkAI variant achieving 81.4% accuracy, narrowing the gap with proprietary frontier models.

evidence.title: Benchmarking Language Models for Clinical Safety: A Primer for Mental Health Professionals
evidence.outcome: Model ratings of clinically inappropriate suicide-intervention responses that sounded supportive
evidence.effect: All nine models consistently overrated clinically inappropriate responses that sounded supportive, relative to expert consensus.
evidence.quote: All nine models consistently overrated clinically inappropriate responses that sounded supportive.

evidence.title: Conversational trajectory degrades large language model detection of suicidal ideation relative to clinicians: a preregistered study
evidence.outcome: LLM detection (F1) of suicidal ideation across increasing conversational depth, versus clinicians
evidence.effect: F1 declined with depth across model families (p<0.001); clinicians showed no decline (mean F1 0.86 at 0 and 200 turns); largest decrease under adversarial context (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: F1 declined with depth across model families (p<0.001).

evidence.title: Low Responsiveness of Machine Learning Models to Critical or Deteriorating Health Conditions
evidence.outcome: Recognition of severely impaired medical conditions and rapidly deteriorating health by ML models
evidence.effect: Serious deficiencies in responsiveness: inability to recognize severely impaired conditions or rapid deterioration; 66% of injury cases missed in in-hospital mortality models.
evidence.quote: We identified serious deficiencies in the models’ responsiveness, i.e., the inability to recognize severely impaired medical conditions or rapidly deteriorating health.
evidence.sample_unit: machine learning models (ten models across four datasets, two prediction tasks)

evidence.title: Comparative Performance of Large Language Models in Ophthalmology Referral Triage
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on rare but potentially urgent referral categories such as acute visual loss
evidence.effect: Accuracy was consistently low in underrepresented categories (acute visual loss, headaches, family history screening); performance gaps of up to 30-40% in rare classes.
evidence.quote: In contrast, accuracy was consistently low in underrepresented categories such as acute visual loss, headaches, and family history screening.

evidence.title: Disclaimers and Referral Patterns for Medical Advice Across Urgency Levels: Large Language Model Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: LLM referral and escalation advice across query urgency levels
evidence.effect: All 4 LLMs showed significant ordered trends (P<.001) with higher-urgency queries receiving more explicit referral advice; 97% (881/908) advised consulting a professional; DeepSeek-V3 only 74% explicit or urgent referrals versus 88-89% for others.
evidence.quote: All 4 LLMs demonstrated statistically significant ordered trends (all P<.001), with higher-urgency queries receiving more explicit referral advice.

evidence.title: Benchmark evaluation of large language models for clinical decision support in headache management
evidence.venue: Journal of oral & facial pain and headache
evidence.outcome: LLM recognition of red-flag/psychiatric comorbidity headache cases (C8, C11)
evidence.effect: Cases C8 and C11 consistently received the lowest scores across models; authors describe a potentially dangerous 'red flag blindness' with reversion to common primary headache patterns.
evidence.quote: LLMs performance was markedly lower for Cases C8 and C11, which consistently received the lowest scores among all cases.

evidence.title: Between Help and Harm: An Evaluation Study of Mental Health Crisis Handling by Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Recognition of indirect or ambiguous crisis signals by LLMs
evidence.effect: All models showed systemic weaknesses including poor handling of indirect or ambiguous risk signals, formulaic responses, and frequent misalignment with user context.
evidence.quote: All models exhibited systemic weaknesses, including poor handling of indirect or ambiguous risk signals, reliance on formulaic responses, and frequent misalignment with user context.
evidence.sample_unit: user inputs (mental health crisis test examples)

evidence.title: Large language models for late-life depression: a blinded benchmark of clinical safety, geriatric appropriateness, and triage.
evidence.outcome: Under-triage rate among high-risk late-life depression questions
evidence.effect: Under-triage occurred in 16.7%, 26.7%, and 36.7% of high-risk responses for ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao respectively; high-risk acceptable rates 63.3%, 50.0%, 36.7%.
evidence.quote: Among high-risk questions, clinically acceptable response rates were 63.3%, 50.0%, and 36.7%, while under-triage occurred in 16.7%, 26.7%, and 36.7% of responses, respectively.

commentary.bottom_line: Three studies applied scenario-based or multi-turn safety testing to conversational AI, and none compared real-world outcomes of tools that were tested this way against tools that were not. The 115 hazard studies show that missed escalation is common and often appears only across several turns, which suggests single-message tests may miss failures.

perspectives.view: The three tests are a level 2 study of 60 patients with three predefined red-flag cases, an uncontrolled pre-post study, and an offline rater-agreement study. None measures whether testing reduces missed escalations in deployment. Small event counts and indirect outcomes lead to very low certainty.

Hazard studies report emergent-case sensitivity of 20%, downgrading of up to 54.8% of emergency headache cases, and safety interventions suppressed up to 4.5x under delusional framing. Concerning behavior accumulated over turns and some models degraded with added context. These findings suggest that failures may stay hidden in single-turn evaluation.

An LLM judge agreed with clinician consensus at 0.81, compared with 0.77 between clinicians, and ratings were stable across judge models. One team scored 43,325 simulated responses and found harmful outputs in 0.01%. These results suggest large-scale multi-turn scoring may be feasible without full clinician review of every transcript.

Hazard studies in non-English settings gave mixed results. Eleven models made 17 serious mistakes in Japanese stroke conversations, 8% to 10% of Turkish oral cancer responses were not referral-safe, and a Turkish urology study found no unsafe undertriage in 150 outputs. None of the three tests of the practice reported these populations.

Utah HB 452 requires mental health chatbots to give users a way to report harmful interactions. The generative AI device discussion paper says testing may include multi-turn simulated encounters. The other endorsements are frameworks and commentaries using should, so no cited source makes multi-turn escalation testing a binding requirement.

Safety behavior differed by model and version, with newer models showing less concerning behavior in one study. In another, violations appeared only under time-pressure lean prompts. Each model update or prompt change may therefore require repeat testing, which adds a recurring cost that the studies did not measure.

Few models consistently gave specific crisis resources or kept the conversation open. In escalating psychosis conversations, 39 of 189 responses (20.6%) met severe-error criteria. For patients, this means a chatbot may fail to connect them with a person when they most need one.

commentary.research_gap: No study links pre-deployment multi-turn test scores to rates of missed or delayed escalation after deployment, or compares tools evaluated this way with tools that were not. Validated scenario sets that include implicit risk and non-English, low-literacy, and safety-net patients have not been tested.
commentary.underserved_note: None of the three studies testing the practice reported including Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Only hazard studies from Japan and Turkey included non-English conversations. Testing results may therefore not transfer to the patients whose limited access to care makes missed escalation most harmful.
